notes: Claude Opus 5.5 launch headline table (Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1 / Opus 5 / GPT-6 Astra / GPT-5.6 Sol), read from the launch page's server-rendered <table> cells — EXACT published values, not digitization. Per-benchmark 'best score' column only (each model's highest reported score across effort, per the page's own note: "Unless otherwise noted, all Claude Opus 5.5 results use adaptive thinking at max effort. Terminal-Bench 4.0 results are reported for Claude Opus 5.5 at xhigh effort and GPT-6 Astra at high effort, as reported by OpenAI; these represent each model's highest score."). GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol figures are AS REPORTED BY OPENAI (Anthropic did not independently rerun them) — do not treat these as Anthropic-measured. Opus 5.5 was evaluated WITH its production safeguards enabled; when they intervened, cybersecurity tasks were completed by Claude Opus 4.8 and biology/frontier-LLM-development tasks by Claude Opus 5, which may reduce Opus 5.5's own scores on those benchmarks. Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode v1.1 (Main), CursorBench 4.0, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench, and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 rows here are the SAME table also carrying full effort-stratified series in the page's inline-SVG chart aria-labels (low/medium/high/xhigh/max per model) — that full effort-curve extraction is a separate chart-digitization task and is NOT ingested in this file; only the single best-score-per-model headline row is recorded here. This launch's Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 rows are DIFFERENT readings from the OpenAI GPT-6 Astra launch page and the secondary tbench.ai audit already held in this pack (performance/openai-gpt-6-astra-launch-2026-09.json, performance/terminal-bench-4-astra-audit-2026-09.json) — three different publishers under nominally the same benchmark name; do not merge or average across files. Footnote 1 (Terminal-Bench 4.0) verbatim: "The standard error is ±2.6 pts for Claude Opus 5.5 and ±1.6–2 pts for the other Claude models. The public leaderboard (5 trials/task, Claude Code harness) reports Claude Opus 5 at 51.8%; our setup reproduces it at 52.3%, within noise. GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol figures are as reported by OpenAI." Footnote 2 (AutomationBench) verbatim: "AutomationBench results were run and reported by Zapier. These runs were performed without fallback models, so safeguard interventions were considered failures—this resulted in a lower score than Claude Opus 5.5 would achieve in practice. Claude Opus 5.5 results come from Zapier's own evaluation during early access. Results for Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra come from Zapier's public leaderboard." Footnote 3 (Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1) verbatim: "The standard error is ±3.5–5 pts per model. The public leaderboard (3 trials/task, Claude Code harness) reports Claude Opus 5 at 30.0%; our setup reproduces it at 29.0%, within noise. The GPT-6 Astra figure is as reported by OpenAI." OSWorld 2.0 and Chartography rows are qualified 'partial'/'with tools' respectively per the source table; no dash-only cells (GPT-6 Astra/GPT-5.6 Sol on OSWorld 2.0 and Chartography) are recorded as scores — they are simply absent, consistent with 'never invent'.

claims.statement: At default effort (medium), Opus 5.5 beats GPT-6 Astra at max effort for about a fifth of the cost per task on FrontierCode v1.1 (Main): "At default effort (medium), Opus 5.5 scores 54.6%, higher than all other models, beating GPT-6 Astra's top score (53.3%) for about a fifth of the cost per task."
claims.implication: Vendor claim, not independently reproduced. Opus 5.5's default effort is medium; GPT-6 Astra's own top score is at its own max, not necessarily medium.

claims.statement: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Opus 5.5 at default effort beats Opus 5 at max effort for about a fifth of the cost; it matches GPT-6 Astra at about 40% of the cost.

On CursorBench 4.0 at default effort (medium), Opus 5.5 scores 52.5%, compared to 51.8% for Fable 5.1 (max) and 46.6% for Opus 5 (max); it beats GPT-5.6 Sol's top score (41.7%) by 11 points for about a third of the cost per task.

Customer quote (unnamed financial firm, BigFinance Bench — not an Anthropic-run public benchmark): "Financial firms need outputs that are consistently correct. At its lowest effort setting, Claude Opus 5.5 beat Opus 5 at high effort on our BigFinance Bench with about 60% fewer output tokens. Its answers are shorter and better structured, and its slides come out denser, more in line with industry standards."
claims.implication: Third-party customer testimonial cited by the vendor, not a published benchmark score; BigFinance Bench is not a public/independent board in this pack. Do not treat as equivalent to a scored row.
